description: Provider-neutral role policy. Resolve with scripts/resolve-model-routing.sh, then copy the result to RUN_DIR/model-routing.json.

claude.note: haiku/sonnet/opus for most defaults; fable reached by escalation, plus the Counselor's standing default — re-enabled Jul 2026. haiku is the cheap rung (Scoot). **Fable is not a review-gate default:** cold reviewers run on a capable tier in a fresh context (roles.delegate.cold_reviewer.tier, normally strong) and escalate to fable only on prior_review_missed_issue or second_critic_loop. Independence is bought by isolation.

openai.note: Codex host: native subagent spawns use gpt-5.6-terra or gpt-5.6-sol by default; gpt-6-astra is reserved for the escalated tier. gpt-5.3-codex-spark is allowed only through the granular-ui-fast one-shot exec profile. Pass model and reasoning effort explicitly on every launch.

grok.note: Grok Bot host: native specialist spawns use grok-4.3 (cheap/standard) or grok-4.6 (strong/frontier/escalated). grok-build-0.1 is exec-only until a one-shot helper exists. Pass model and reasoning effort explicitly on every launch. Live transport is Grok Bot Task/executor (GROK.md); scripts/run-grok-specialist.sh --plan is the audit record.

escalation_ladder.applies_to: the role that produced the rejected work — the FIXER, not the reviewer
escalation_ladder.note: Robin, 2026-09-16. Cursor-only replacement of the global two-rung ladder. Grok 4.6 (frontier, Cursor Models pool) is cheaper than Opus 5 (escalated, Other Models), so the fixer tries Grok on the second bounce and Opus only on the third. After the third try fails, escalate to Robin — no fourth model. Challenger / Delegate cold reviewer / Notary miss-escalation still uses the global reviewer table (escalated = Opus), not this fixer ladder.

cursor.note: Cursor Agent host: native specialist spawns use Task-tool slugs from config/runtimes/cursor.json. inherit is forbidden. Live transport is Cursor Task (CURSOR.md); scripts/run-cursor-specialist.sh --plan is the audit record. Cloud Task is opt-in and does not replace local cold review. Fixer bounces use host_policy.cursor.escalation_ladder (Sol → Grok 4.6 → Opus), not the global two-rung jump to escalated.

granular-ui-fast.description: Fast first-pass implementation for a bounded, text-only change to one existing frontend surface.

challenger.note: Cold review is bought by FRESH CONTEXT: a reviewer that has not seen the design argued gives real objections. fresh_context_required is the invariant. QA runs on a sufficiently capable tier and escalates only on a demonstrated miss. Robin, 2026-09-16. Regression specs 13 and 295 assert this shape; do not reintroduce author-derived routing.

cleric.note: The Cleric drives design-taste-frontend (tasteskill) and impeccable, so it is a thinker on the strong tier (Robin, 2026-09-16). Design direction and the pre-ship quality gate are judgement work, not handoff transcription.

counselor.note: The Counselor runs FABLE by default (Robin, 2026-09-16) — the one deliberate exception to 'fable for escalation only'. Two reasons it is not an escalation case. Voice, audience framing and persuasion are the work fable is actually better at, unlike code where opus and the gates carry it. And it is the only role in the cast whose miss is not recoverable by a fix round: everywhere else a bad output is caught by a gate, a test, or a bounce that escalates the fixer, but copy that ships under Robin's name has already left when anyone notices. Spawns are rare (pre-send review), so the aggregate cost is small. 'cheap' is removed from allowed: nothing about this role wants haiku.

systemsmith.note: The Systemsmith is a thinker, not a grunt: it writes production code over durable state, which is where this campaign's pair-shaped defects are authored (Robin, 2026-09-16). A cheaper coder moves cost sideways into fix rounds — rheo-stream 0c2 bounced 5 of 5 chunks, 12 coder spawns for five chunks, and each bounce costs a spawn plus a review. second_challenger_rejection escalates it a rung further.

cold_reviewer.note: The per-checkpoint cold reviewer runs on a capable tier in a FRESH CONTEXT. Independence is bought by isolation; rheo-stream 0c2 measured an opus reviewer finding 9 blockers where a fable one found 1 on the same artifacts at the same cost. Escalation follows a demonstrated miss. The Delegate passes the tier's model via BUREAU_REVIEWER_MODEL and logs a MODEL-OVERRIDE when it differs from roles.delegate.model. Robin, 2026-09-16; regression spec 13 asserts this shape.

escalation_ladder.applies_to: the role that produced the rejected work — the FIXER, not the reviewer
escalation_ladder.note: Robin, 2026-09-16. A bounce is evidence the work item is harder than assumed, and the role that produced it is where that difficulty lives — so the FIXER escalates, not the reviewer. Targets are named rather than expressed as 'one rung up', because 'one rung' has to be inferred from the tier order and a role already at strong then has two possible readings. A role whose default already meets or exceeds a rung's target stays where it is. Declared here AND in docs/model-routing-and-cast.md; the Conductor and Delegate apply it at specialist retry dispatch and log a MODEL-OVERRIDE naming the trigger. This replaces the older 'bounce rule, one rung on the second rejection', which named no target tier. Cursor replaces this ladder at resolve time with host_policy.cursor.escalation_ladder (second bounce → frontier / Grok 4.6, third → escalated / Opus). Claude and Codex keep these two rungs.
